findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — `prisma.credential.update()` called but `prisma` is never imported — `ReferenceError` on every `SalesforceCalendarService` construction; does not compile. That this reached the branch implies type-check/build is not gating this package.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97-101 — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod **safeParse wrapper**, not `.data`; `key` is written to `credential.key` as `{"success":true,"data":{…}}`. Next load throws in `googleCredentialSchema.parse` (line 75) → Google credential permanently unusable, no self-heal, no `invalid` flag. Occurs sync-enabled **or not**. Other callers (o365 `:264`, salesforce `:98`) correctly unwrap `.data` — Google is the outlier.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11 — `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal key `"[object Object]"`; the second overwrites the first. Effective schema is `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown }`. The documented "any numeric property is the expiry" rule does not exist, and because zod strips unknown keys, `.data` is reduced to `{ access_token }` — expiry, `instance_url`, `refresh_token`, scope are all discarded before persistence. A validator that is green while validating nothing.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27 — Unconditionally injects the **literal string** `"refresh_token"` when `data.refresh_token` is falsy. At `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264` the spread puts `data` last, so the real stored refresh token is clobbered and persisted. Fires in the non-sync path too (`refresh_token` is `.optional()` in `refreshTokenResponseSchema:56`), and is guaranteed in sync mode since #3 strips it. One-way door: once written, the real token is gone; disabling the feature does not recover it and no backfill is provided.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — Sync branch returns a raw `fetch` `Response`; fallback returns the app's parsed result. Two call sites cannot handle it: **google** `:94` does `res?.data` → `undefined` → `TypeError`, swallowed by the `catch` at `:102` (message ≠ `invalid_grant`) so refresh silently no-ops forever; **hubspot** `:177-197` casts the `Response` to `HubspotToken`, computes `expiryDate = NaN`, and writes the `Response` into `credential.key`, destroying the credential — also swallowed by `catch`. Lark/o365-calendar/o365-video/webex survive only incidentally (their refreshFunction also returns a `Response`); nothing enforces that invariant.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29 — If `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset, a request that omits the header yields `undefined !== undefined` → false → **the auth check passes**. Combined with fully attacker-controlled `userId` (`:11`) and `appSlug`, an unauthenticated caller can create or overwrite any user's credential for any app. No fail-closed guard, no rate limit. *Reachability depends on how `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is derived — `packages/lib/constants.ts` is absent from this checkout, so this is P0-if-reachable.*

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30-59 — The `state?.teamId` branch returns at `:56`, so the sole `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` call at `:59` is reached **only** when `teamId` is falsy and is always passed `null` — dead code. The team branch itself checks only `members: { some: { userId, accepted: true } }` with **no role filter**. Any accepted team member can bind a team-wide Stripe/Salesforce/HubSpot/Webex/Tandem/MS-Teams credential (e.g. payment redirection via `stripepayment/api/callback.ts:44`). `select: { members }` is fetched and unused.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-108 — Three compounding defects: (a) refreshes on **every** service construction with no expiry check — one extra token grant per availability/booking op; (b) the refreshed token is persisted but the `jsforce.Connection` at `:101` is still built from the **stale** `credentialKey.access_token`/`instance_url`, so the refresh has no effect on the current request; (c) it bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens` entirely, so Salesforce silently never participates in credential sync while still being validated by the weakened schema from #3 (which strips `instance_url`). Also `this.conn = this.getClient(...)` at `:57` has no `.catch` → unhandled rejection on the new network/DB failure modes.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15 — The sync `fetch` has no `AbortSignal`/timeout, no `response.ok` check, no retry, no try/catch. A hung partner endpoint blocks token refresh on the booking critical path until platform timeout; a 500/HTML body is passed straight to `handleErrorsJson`/`handleLarkError`/`handleWebexResponse`, none of which is wrapped in try/catch at the call site. No circuit breaking — a flapping endpoint fails every calendar operation.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15` vs `refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 — Gating is mismatched: `refreshOAuthTokens` additionally requires `userId`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` does not. For **team** credentials (`userId === null`) on a sync-enabled deployment, the refresh correctly hits the real provider but the response is then stripped by the minimum schema and given the placeholder refresh token — team credentials are silently destroyed by a feature documented as user-only.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — No `req.method` check — `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE`/`HEAD` all reach the credential-write path. Compare `zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:33`, which does return `400 Invalid request method`. Defeats method-based CSRF/WAF/proxy assumptions on a state-mutating public endpoint.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31, 57-59 — `schema.parse` (not `safeParse`), `symmetricDecrypt`, and `JSON.parse` of the plaintext are all unguarded in a raw handler with no `defaultResponder`. A malformed body, a mismatched `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, or non-JSON plaintext each produce an opaque 500 + stack instead of the route's `{ message }` 400 shape — the caller cannot distinguish "bad key" from "bad payload" from "server broken", making retry logic impossible.

packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:86-94 — `key: responseBody` replaces the credential **wholesale** and never merges with the prior key or routes through `parseRefreshTokenResponse`. In sync mode the endpoint returns only access token + expiry, so `refresh_token` is dropped and the MS Teams credential can never refresh again. No try/catch — the failure lands in video-link creation during booking.

packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:62,88`; `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:67,83 — Both opt into `refreshOAuthTokens` but then validate with schemas the documented sync contract ("access token and expiry only") cannot satisfy: `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` requires `refresh_token`, `refresh_token_expires_in`, `token_type: literal("Bearer")` and a `scope` **literal**; Lark's `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>` expects a nested `data.data.{…}` envelope. Every sync refresh rejects with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned".

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:21-23 — The helper **throws** on failure but replaced `schema.safeParse(...)`, and callers still branch on `.success`: `salesforce:92-94` (`if (!accessTokenParsed.success) return Promise.reject(...)`) and `office365calendar:264` (`tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data`) are both dead. The diff also deleted o365's `console.error("Outlook error grabbing new tokens ~ zodError:", …, responseJson)`, replacing a message naming the app plus the zod error and raw MS payload with one generic app-agnostic string shared by all 8 apps — token-refresh debuggability across the app store is materially worse.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86 — `if (response.statusText !== "OK")` — `statusText` is empty under HTTP/2 (which `login.salesforce.com` serves), so successful refreshes throw `HttpError(400, "")` with an undiagnosable empty message; conversely a non-200 with statusText "OK" slips through. Use `response.ok`.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:9`, `encodeOAuthState.ts:9 — Unguarded `JSON.parse(req.query.state)` with no schema validation, result cast to `IntegrationOAuthCallbackState` by assertion. A malformed `?state=` 500s every OAuth callback (9 call sites), and in `createOAuthAppCredential` it throws *after* the token exchange. `stripepayment/api/callback.ts:11-17` wraps the identical parse in try/catch — the shared helper is a regression against that. Unvalidated `state.teamId` flows straight into the authz query at `createOAuthAppCredential.ts:34`. Also: `encodeOAuthState` returns `undefined` when state is absent, and callers interpolate it directly, producing a literal `state=undefined` that later throws in decode.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-90 — `findFirst`-then-create/update with no transaction, upsert, or `orderBy`: concurrent syncs both see no row and both `create`, yielding duplicates; with pre-existing duplicates an arbitrary row is updated. The `update` sets only `key` and never clears `invalid`, so once `googlecalendar:112-117` flips `invalid: true`, pushing a valid credential returns `200 "Credentials updated"` while the credential stays disabled forever. The query also filters on `userId` only, so a **team**-scoped credential is never matched — the webhook silently creates a second, user-scoped credential instead of updating it.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:5-11` → `createOAuthAppCredential.ts:28 — OAuth `state` is a plain data envelope: no nonce, no session binding, no signature on encode; nothing verified on decode. Since callbacks trust `state.teamId` as the authorization target, a logged-in victim induced to hit `/api/integrations/<app>/callback?code=<attacker>&state={"teamId":N}` links an attacker-controlled provider account to a resource of the attacker's choosing (OAuth account-linking CSRF).

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29 — Secret compared with short-circuiting `!==` rather than `crypto.timingSafeEqual` — a timing oracle on the only credential guarding an endpoint that writes arbitrary users' OAuth keys.

*(whole diff)*

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — Node lowercases incoming header keys, so any uppercase in `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` makes the lookup permanently `undefined` → every sync request 403s. Only a prose comment in `.env.example` guards this; normalize with `.toLowerCase()`. Fails closed, but silently.
8 call sites + `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17`

refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15`, `app-credential.ts:19,25 — The `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` gate is duplicated verbatim in two files and checked differently in a third; four new env vars are read ad hoc from `process.env` rather than surfaced through `@calcom/lib/constants`. Setting one without the other silently no-ops with no startup validation and no warning.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15 — Outbound sync POST carries no `Authorization`, no signature, no `Content-Type`, and no `https://` scheme enforcement, yet the response is expected to contain a live access token that gets persisted. Any party who can reach that endpoint can request a token for an arbitrary `calcomUserId`. Not SSRF (URL is operator-configured, verified). Recommend signing with `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, symmetric to the inbound webhook.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:9-11 — Parses then immediately re-stringifies the same value — a no-op round-trip whose only observable effects are throwing on malformed JSON and key-order normalization. The name promises an encoding step the body does not perform.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:6 — Imports `"../oauth/decodeOAuthState"` from inside `_utils/oauth/` instead of `"./decodeOAuthState"` — resolves fine, but a mechanical-rewrite artifact that will mislead the next reader.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:81,91 — Success returns only an interpolated human string (`Credentials updated for userId: 42`) with no machine-readable create/update discriminator; path is unversioned; the request contract exists only as inline comments plus `.env.example` prose — no exported schema, OpenAPI entry, or docs for a boundary external systems are explicitly expected to call.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97`, `office365calendar:263`, `salesforce:90 — Behavioral widening with no test adjustment: a strict `.parse()`/`safeParse()` was swapped for `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, which substitutes the near-empty minimum schema whenever the two env vars are set. Any existing suite asserting that a malformed refresh response is rejected now covers strictly less than before, without a single test file changing.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29 — Secret compared with short-circuiting `!==` rather than `crypto.timingSafeEqual` — a timing oracle on the only credential guarding an endpoint that writes arbitrary users' OAuth keys.

adjudication.rationale:
The new webhook handler authorizes requests solely by checking a shared secret header:

```ts
if (req.headers[... ] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET) return 403
```

This is a normal JS `!==` string comparison, not a constant‑time comparison. Because this secret is the only guard before the endpoint decrypts input and updates/creates credentials for an arbitrary `userId`+`appSlug` in the database, the finding correctly identifies a verifiable security weakness in the diff: the comparison is potentially timing‑leaky and could be replaced with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` to avoid timing oracle risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — Node lowercases incoming header keys, so any uppercase in `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` makes the lookup permanently `undefined` → every sync request 403s. adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the code indexes `req.headers[...]` using `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` verbatim. In Node/Next, `req.headers` keys are normalized to lowercase, and object property access is case-sensitive. So if an operator sets `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` to a mixed/uppercase value (e.g. `Calcom-Webhook-Secret`), `req.headers[thatValue]` will be `undefined`, causing the secret check to fail and the endpoint to always 403. The `.env.example` comment advises lowercase but the code doesn’t enforce it (no `.toLowerCase()`), so this is a real, diff-introduced misconfiguration trap.
